q.description: Parameter defines the query you want to search. You can use anything that you would use in a regular DuckDuckGo Images search. (e.g., `site:`) Parameter length can not exceed 500 characters.

kl.description: Parameter defines the region to use for the DuckDuckGo Images search. Region code examples: `us-en` (default) for the United States, `uk-en` for United Kingdom, or `fr-fr` for France. Head to the DuckDuckGo regions for a full list of supported regions.

safe.description: Parameter defines the level of filtering for adult content. It can be set to `1` (Strict), `-1` (Moderate - default), or `-2` (Off).

df.description: Parameter defines results filtered by date. It can be set to: `d` - Past day `w` - Past week `m` - Past month `y` - Past year

size.description: Parameter defines results filtered by image size. It can be set to: `Small` - Small `Medium` - Medium `Large` - Large `Wallpaper` - Wallpaper

color.description: Parameter defines results filtered by image color. It can be set to: `color` - Color only `Monochrome` - Black and white `Red` - Red `Orange` - Orange `Yellow` - Yellow `Green` - Green `Blue` - Blue `Purple` - Purple `Pink` - Pink `Brown` - Brown `Black` - Black `Gray` - Gray `Teal` - Teal `White` - White

image_type.description: Parameter defines results filtered by image type. It can be set to: `photo` - Photograph `clipart` - Clipart `gif` - Animated GIF `transparent` - Transparent `line` - Line drawing

layout.description: Parameter defines results filtered by image layout. It can be set to: `Square` - Square `Tall` - Tall `Wide` - Wide

license.description: Parameter defines results filtered by image license. It can be set to: `Any` - All Creative Commons `Public` - Public domain `Share` - Free to share and use `ShareCommercially` - Free to share and use commercially `Modify` - Free to modify, share, and use `ModifyCommercially` - Free to modify, share, and use commercially

hide_ai_images.description: Parameter defines whether to hide AI-generated images, like DuckDuckGo's Hide AI images setting. It can be set to `true` or `false` (default).

start.description: Parameter defines the result offset. It skips the given number of results. DuckDuckGo Images returns up to 100 `images_results` per page, so the next page starts at `100`. The next page can be found in the SerpApi JSON response: `serpapi_pagination -> next`

engine.description: Set parameter to `duckduckgo_images` to use the DuckDuckGo Images API engine.

no_cache.description: Parameter will force SerpApi to fetch the DuckDuckGo Images results even if a cached version is already present. A cache is served only if the query and all parameters are exactly the same. Cache expires after 1h. Cached searches are free, and are not counted towards your searches per month. It can be set to `false` (default) to allow results from the cache, or `true` to disallow results from the cache. no_cache and async parameters should not be used together.

async.description: Parameter defines the way you want to submit your search to SerpApi. It can be set to `false` (default) to open an HTTP connection and keep it open until you got your search results, or `true` to just submit your search to SerpApi and retrieve them later. In this case, you'll need to use our Searches Archive API to retrieve your results. async and no_cache parameters should not be used together. async should not be used on accounts with Ludicrous Speed enabled.

zero_trace.description: Enterprise only. Parameter enables ZeroTrace mode. It can be set to `false` (default) or `true`. Enable this mode to skip storing search parameters, search files, and search metadata on our servers. This may make debugging more difficult.

api_key.description: Parameter defines the SerpApi private key to use.

output.description: Parameter defines the format of the result. It can be set to `json` (default) to get a structured JSON of the results, `html` to get the raw HTML retrieved, or `md` to get a Markdown-formatted version optimized for LLMs and AI agents.

json_restrictor.description: Parameter defines the fields you want to include in the output, reducing payload size for faster response. See the JSON Restrictor documentation for more details.
